title: sm: worked the wrong way round
summary: A product card written with sm: as if it meant phones stacks on desktop and sits side by side on a phone. Tailwind breakpoints mean that width and up, so plain classes are for phones and md: is for wider screens.

turns.user: product card. wanted it stacked on phones only so i put sm:flex-col, but phones are still side by side and desktop stacks

assistant.body: Great question! sm:flex-col comes before flex-row in the class list, so flex-row, which comes later, overrides it. Move the sm: class to the end and phones will stack.
<article class="flex flex-row gap-4 rounded-lg border p-4 sm:flex-col">

Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. The order inside a class attribute has no effect. What wins is the order in the stylesheet, and Tailwind emits sm: classes after the plain ones. So sm:flex-col was working all along. The real cause is what sm: means. It is not for phones: it applies at 40rem, which is 640px, and wider. Tailwind is mobile first. A plain class applies at every width, phones included, and a prefixed class overrides it from its width up. In other words, write the phone layout with plain classes and add md: for wider screens. md: starts at 48rem, 768px.

turns.user: fixed. hmm but on an iPad in portrait side by side is cramped. make the row start at lg. description can still show from md

assistant.body: Sure. Only the row and the image width move up to lg:, which starts at 64rem, 1024px. The heading and the description keep md:, so a portrait iPad gets the stacked card with its description. Here's the takeaway: each class can switch at its own breakpoint.
